items.title: Strophoid
paragraphs: The curve is symmetric about the x-axis. At the origin its lowest-degree equation is \(ay^2=3ax^2\), so the tangents are \(y=\pm\sqrt3x\): the origin is a node.
Putting y=0 gives x=0 or x=3a. The factor (a+x) in the denominator of \(y^2=x^2(3a-x)/(a+x)\) gives the vertical asymptote x=−a. Real points require \(-a<x\le3a\).
Implicit differentiation gives \(2y(a+x)y\prime+y^2=6ax-3x^2\). Substitute the value of y² and simplify:

On the upper loop branch, y′>0 for \(0<x<\sqrt3a\), and y′<0 for \(\sqrt3a<x<3a\); reflect in the x-axis for the lower loop. At (3a,0) the tangent is vertical. For −a<x<0 the upper branch decreases toward the node and the lower branch is its reflection.
items.final_answer: A loop lies between x=0 and x=3a, with two unbounded branches approaching x=−a.
